Title: 'Improving the quality of life'
NewsSummary: "It is a chance to live a normal life," said 28-year-old Rabia, a recent participant of the Aga Khan University Hospital's new kidney transplant programme speaking at an awareness session for people with chronic kidney disease.

content.text: "It is a chance to live a normal life," said 28-year-old Rabia, a recent participant of the Aga Khan University Hospital's new kidney transplant programme speaking at an awareness session for people with chronic kidney disease. "My options were limited to dialysis, as long as it was possible, or a kidney transplant. This is a new lease on life."

Rabia's willingness to speak about her experience of receiving a kidney from her mother was an opportunity for patients with end-stage renal failure to hear first-hand about the transplant process and to adjusting to life with a new kidney.

For kidney patients attending the University Hospital's awareness session, this was also an opportunity to receive advice and information about kidney transplants, and to attend a free screening clinic where a trained team of nephrologists evaluated their potential for surgery.

"Every patient with advanced kidney disease, whether diabetic or not, should be evaluated for a kidney transplant as the quality of life is far better," said Dr Waqar Kashif, Associate Professor and Head of Nephrology at the University Hospital. "We can manage surgeries for a variety of age groups and provide comprehensive care."

At AKUH, a highly specialized multi-disciplinary team of experts with access to state-of-the-art laboratory, pharmacy and radiology services backs the kidney transplant programme. Dr Abdul Mabood Khalil, Assistant Professor, Section of Nephrology, spoke of the extensive pre-transplant evaluation process and the post-transplant consultations where the patient and donor are closely monitored, supported and managed through the recovery period. Even after discharge, the patient and donor continue to have access to regular up-to-date advice and information.

Also speaking on the occasion, Professor Taqi Khan, with extensive experience of performing transplant surgeries in USA, as well as Middle and Far East shared his knowledge of transplant surgeries and was later available to answer questions from the audience.
